newsitem.title: UK: Stock increase on LME knocks wind out of copper.
newsitem.headline: Stock increase on LME knocks wind out of copper.

text.p: The first rise in London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouse stocks of copper since early September knocked the wind out of prices, as the increase may be the first sign of the market toppling over.
Stocks rose 2,425 tonnes to 92,475 tonnes, knocking prices some $25 lower to $2,230 a tonne. But the market is expected to remain volatile over the next few weeks, traders said.
"I think it is too early to say that this is the first cuckoo of spring. The next month is still going to be very rocky," one said.
"Maybe the shenanigans on the LME are drawing to an end and we can now focus on the true picture, which is that galloping surpluses lie ahead," analyst Nick Moore of the Flemings Global Mining Group.
In the short-term, traders said there is still widespread uncertainty over stock movements, concern over December options, and severe technical tightness in the middle of next month.
But now that the run of stock drawdowns has been broken, the talked-about increases of some 20,000 tonnes before the year-end may be taking place, they noted.
The LME reported on Friday that 5,425 tonnes of copper had been delivered into the key Singapore warehouse, while 1,100 tonnes was shipped out.
Meanwhile, in the U.S. 2,375 tonnes was delivered into Long Beach, while 1,275 tonnes was removed. Elsewhere, copper stocks showed a net fall in the European warehouses.
Given the raging backwardation on the LME, the London market has moved to a substantial premium over COMEX in New York.
"Clearly, there has been some stock re-distribution from the COMEX warehouses to LME," Moore said.

Copper's cash/threes backwardation was calmer on Friday, narrowing to $240 after hitting a high point of $285 on Thursday, when the forward market peaked at $2,213 - the highest since the Sumitomo Corp scandal erupted in June 1996.
In the short-term, the market has Wednesday's December options to contend with, as there are large upside calls at the $2,500 and $2,600 strikes.
Then, the critical period for tightness is December 16/18 when substantial short positions will need to be covered or rolled forward.
Until these hurdles are cleared, prices will remain volatile, and Thursday's highs could well be tested once again.
"The copper price outlook is one of pinnacles and ravines. At the moment we are in a ravine," Moore said.
